findings.title: Mixed admin and user handoffs bypass user write fencing
findings.description: An admin handoff persists stcontrolAdmin in the browser session, a later user handoff does not clear it, and the request tracker skips every user fence whenever that marker exists.
findings.recommendation: Make handoff roles mutually exclusive: end and clear the user envelope before an admin handoff, clear stcontrolAdmin before a user handoff, and add a mixed-handoff regression test.
findings.impact: A mixed-role browser session can issue user writes without stale-writer lease checks, snapshot/data-fault gates, or independent reconciliation fencing.

findings.title: OAuth login state is not bound to the initiating browser
findings.description: Login-purpose OAuth state stores only its hash, provider, optional node, and generation; callback redemption proves no browser cookie or pre-auth session binding.
findings.recommendation: Set a host-only HttpOnly SameSite=Lax callback-scoped cookie at OAuth begin and require a constant-time exact match before consuming login-purpose state; keep the existing session-bound identity-link flow unchanged.
references: OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice - CSRF Protection
findings.impact: A valid callback URL can be completed in a different browser, causing login CSRF, account confusion, or attacker-identity enrollment in the victim session.

cross_references.reason: The same sticky role marker was independently confirmed as a correctness and requirements-coverage defect.
